description: Creation, modification, deletion, enablement, disablement, password, and lockout-related account administration.

source.note: Validate provider, channel, event version, and field names against collected event XML.

4720.headline: A new user account was created
4720.plain_english: A new login account was created on this computer. This is normal during onboarding, but if nobody expected it an intruder may be setting up a way to log in.
4720.technical_description: Security event 4720: a user account object was created. Records the creator (SubjectUserName) and the new account (TargetUserName).

who.SubjectUserName: Account that created the new user

where.Computer: Machine where the account was created

4720.why_it_matters: New accounts are how people gain access. Unrecognized accounts are a common persistence mechanism.
normal_when: A provisioning script creating service accounts
A change ticket exists for the creation
suspicious_when: Created outside business hours
Created by an account that normally doesn't manage users
New account added to Administrators shortly after (see 4732/4728)
Name resembles an existing account (look-alike account)
what_to_do: Ask the person listed as creator whether they created this account
Check whether the new account was added to any admin group
If unrecognized: disable the account and start incident response

severity.high: New account added to an admin group, or correlated with other suspicious activity

4720.important_note: A single account creation is not proof of compromise — context (creator, timing, follow-up) matters.

4722.headline: A user account was enabled
4722.plain_english: A disabled login was turned back on. If you didn't ask for this, someone may be trying to reuse an old or suspended account.
4722.technical_description: Security event 4722: a user account was re-enabled.

where.Computer: Machine where the change was recorded

4722.why_it_matters: Re-enabling an old account can revive access that was deliberately revoked.
normal_when: An account was temporarily suspended for HR reasons and reinstated
suspicious_when: Account was disabled for cause and is re-enabled without a ticket
Re-enabled by an account that normally doesn't manage users
Immediately followed by a 4624 logon for that account
what_to_do: Review any logons that follow (4624) for the account

severity.high: Re-enable of a disabled admin account, or re-enable followed by unusual logon

4722.important_note: Re-enable alone is neutral — the follow-up activity determines risk.

4723.headline: Someone tried to change an account password
4723.plain_english: Someone tried to change a password. Because changing requires knowing the current password, this is usually the user themselves.
4723.technical_description: Security event 4723: change password attempt (requires knowing the current password).

where.Computer: Machine where the change was recorded

4723.when: Time Windows recorded the change attempt.
4723.why_it_matters: If a password change wasn't initiated by the account owner, it can indicate a compromised account.
normal_when: A user changing their own password at password-expiry
suspicious_when: Account owner denies requesting the change
Change followed by unusual logons
Repeated password-change attempts on a service account
what_to_do: Ask the account owner if they requested the change
If denied, treat the account as compromised and reset credentials

severity.high: Change followed by suspicious logon activity

4723.important_note: Password change requires knowing the old password — a change is a weaker signal than a reset (4724).

4724.headline: An administrator reset a user's password
4724.plain_english: An administrator reset a user's password. This is normal when a user forgets it, but if the user didn't ask, someone may have reset it to take over the account.
4724.technical_description: Security event 4724: password reset performed by an administrator (does not require knowing the old password).

where.Computer: Machine where the reset was recorded

4724.why_it_matters: A reset is a common takeover technique because the attacker doesn't need the old password.
suspicious_when: Reset not requested by the user
Reset by an unusual admin account
Reset immediately followed by a logon from an unusual IP
what_to_do: Review subsequent logons (4624) for that account

severity.high: Reset followed by suspicious activity, or reset of a privileged account

4724.important_note: A reset is a stronger signal than a change because it does not require the old password.

4725.headline: A user account was disabled
4725.plain_english: A user account was disabled — the user can no longer sign in until re-enabled.
4725.technical_description: Security event 4725: a user account was disabled.

where.Computer: Machine where the change was recorded

4725.why_it_matters: Disabling can be routine offboarding or a security containment step.
suspicious_when: Mass disable of many accounts at once
Admin account disabled without a ticket
Disable of a service account that then breaks systems
what_to_do: Confirm with HR/IT that the disable was authorized
Check whether affected systems depend on the account

severity.high: Mass disable or disable of critical admin account

4725.important_note: Disabling is not by itself malicious but can be a prelude to cover-up or disruption.

4726.headline: A user account was deleted
4726.plain_english: A user account was deleted. This is destructive — the account and its access are gone. Verify this was authorized.
4726.technical_description: Security event 4726: a user account was deleted.

where.Computer: Machine where the deletion was recorded

4726.why_it_matters: Deletion can remove the audit trail of what the account had access to, and is hard to undo.
suspicious_when: Deleted without backup or ticket
Mass deletion
Deletion by an account that normally doesn't manage users
what_to_do: Confirm with HR/IT that deletion was authorized
Check recent logons by the deleted account for context

severity.high: Mass deletion or deletion of a recently-used account

4726.important_note: Deletion is hard to reverse; verify authorization before assuming legitimate.

4727.headline: A global security group was created
4727.plain_english: A new global security group was created. Global groups are used to grant access across the domain.
4727.technical_description: Security event 4727: security-enabled global group was created.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the event

4727.why_it_matters: Groups are how permissions are bundled; unfamiliar groups can grant unexpected access.
suspicious_when: Group created with admin-sounding name
Created off-hours
Members added immediately (4728)
what_to_do: Confirm with AD admin that the group was requested

severity.high: Group created with admin-like name or immediately populated

4727.important_note: Context (who created it, members added) matters more than the creation alone.

4728.headline: Someone was added to a global security group
4728.plain_english: Someone was added to a global security group. This is how Windows grants permissions — if the group is sensitive (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins), the member now has significant access.
4728.technical_description: Security event 4728: a member was added to a security-enabled global group.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

4728.why_it_matters: Privilege escalation in AD is usually done by adding to an admin group.
suspicious_when: Add to Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, or Schema Admins without a ticket
Off-hours add
Member from a service account that doesn't normally need that access
what_to_do: For sensitive groups, verify with AD admin and review the member's subsequent activity

severity.medium: Unexplained add to a moderate-privilege group
severity.high: Add to a highly privileged admin group

4728.important_note: Sensitivity depends entirely on the group name — Admin groups need immediate review.

4729.headline: Someone was removed from a global security group
4729.plain_english: Someone was removed from a global security group. This revokes access.
4729.technical_description: Security event 4729: a member was removed from a security-enabled global group.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the removal

4729.why_it_matters: Removal can be legitimate offboarding or an attempt to disrupt an account.
suspicious_when: Removed from admin group without a ticket
Mass removal
Removal of the sole owner of a resource
what_to_do: Check whether the affected account still needs this access

severity.high: Removal from a sensitive group disrupting operations

4729.important_note: Removal from sensitive groups can indicate sabotage or containment.

4732.headline: Someone was added to a local security group
4732.plain_english: Someone was added to a local security group on this computer. If the group is Administrators, the member now has full control over this machine.
4732.technical_description: Security event 4732: a member was added to a security-enabled local group. The local Administrators group is the highest-value target.

target.GroupName: Group that was changed (Administrators is high-value)

where.Computer: Machine where the add was recorded

4732.why_it_matters: Adding to local Administrators is one of the most common privilege-escalation steps.
normal_when: Adding a service account with documented purpose
suspicious_when: Add to Administrators without a ticket
Add performed off-hours
Add of an account that also appears in 4624 from an unusual source
what_to_do: For Administrators group, review the member's subsequent activity (4624, 4688)

severity.high: Add to local Administrators without a ticket

4732.important_note: Local Administrators is a common persistence route — take seriously.

4733.headline: Someone was removed from a local security group
4733.plain_english: Someone was removed from a local security group on this computer. This revokes local access.
4733.technical_description: Security event 4733: a member was removed from a security-enabled local group.

where.Computer: Machine where the removal was recorded

4733.why_it_matters: Removal from local Administrators can break workflows or indicate cleanup.
suspicious_when: Mass removal
Removal off-hours
Removal that breaks expected operations

severity.high: Removal of the only admin account on a critical machine

4733.important_note: Removal from a local admin group can be sabotage or can leave a system unmanageable.

4735.headline: A local security group was changed
4735.plain_english: A local security group's properties were changed. This usually means a name or description, not membership.
4735.technical_description: Security event 4735: a security-enabled local group's properties were changed.

where.Computer: Machine where the change was recorded

4735.why_it_matters: Property changes alone rarely grant new access but can be part of disguising changes.
normal_when: Admin renaming a group for clarity
suspicious_when: Renaming a group to look like another
Renaming a sensitive group

severity.high: Change to an admin-sounding group without a ticket

4735.important_note: Property changes are low signal in isolation — look for correlated membership changes.

4737.headline: A global security group was changed
4737.plain_english: A global security group's properties were changed.
4737.technical_description: Security event 4737: a security-enabled global group's properties were changed.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

4737.why_it_matters: Property changes rarely grant access directly but can disguise other changes.
suspicious_when: Renaming a group to mimic another
Unexplained rename of a sensitive group

severity.high: Change to a sensitive group without a ticket

4737.important_note: Property changes should be reviewed together with membership changes.

4738.headline: A user account was changed
4738.plain_english: A user account's properties were modified — this could be a name change, description update, or other attribute. If unexpected, review what changed.
4738.technical_description: Security event 4738: a user account object was modified. The 'Changed Attributes' field (when present) shows what was modified.

where.Computer: Machine where the change was recorded

4738.why_it_matters: Some attribute changes (e.g. 'User Cannot Change Password', account expiry) can enable or disable access.
normal_when: User updating their own contact details
suspicious_when: Change to sensitive flags like 'password never expires'
Change performed by an unexpected account
Change of an admin account

severity.high: Change that alters account security flags or applies to a privileged account

4738.important_note: Review the Changed Attributes field for the actual modification.

4739.headline: The domain password or lockout policy was changed
4739.plain_english: The domain's password or lockout policy was changed. This affects every user in the domain. If unexpected, treat it as high priority — a weaker policy undermines every account.
4739.technical_description: Security event 4739: domain policy was changed (password policy, lockout policy, Kerberos policy, etc.).

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

4739.why_it_matters: Weakening password policy applies domain-wide — this is a serious security event.
suspicious_when: Password length reduced or lockout threshold raised
Off-hours change
Change with no matching change ticket

severity.high: Weaker password or lockout settings applied without authorization

4739.important_note: Any change here affects the whole domain's security posture.

4742.headline: A computer account was changed
4742.plain_english: A computer's domain account was changed. This can be routine (renaming a machine) or malicious (hijacking a computer's domain identity).
4742.technical_description: Security event 4742: a computer account was changed.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

4742.why_it_matters: Computer account hijacking can be used for machine-account attacks in AD.
suspicious_when: Change of an unexpected machine account
Change by a non-admin account

severity.high: Change by an unusual account on a sensitive machine

4742.important_note: Computer account abuse is less common but important in AD environments.

4744.headline: A distribution (non-security) local group was created
4744.plain_english: A distribution group (used for email lists, not access control) was created locally.
4744.technical_description: Security event 4744: security-disabled local group created. Distribution groups do not grant access.

where.Computer: Machine where the group was created

4744.why_it_matters: Distribution groups don't grant resource access, so lower risk than security groups.
suspicious_when: Unexplained group with admin-sounding name

severity.high: Group created by an unexpected account

4744.important_note: Distribution groups do not grant access — lower priority than 4727.

4745.headline: A distribution (non-security) local group was changed
4745.plain_english: A distribution (non-security) local group's properties were changed.
4745.technical_description: Security event 4745: security-disabled local group changed.

where.Computer: Machine where the change was recorded

4745.why_it_matters: Distribution group changes usually affect only email.
suspicious_when: Unexplained changes

severity.high: Change to a group used by an admin process

4745.important_note: Distribution groups do not grant access.

4746.headline: Someone was added to a distribution local group
4746.plain_english: Someone was added to a distribution (non-security) local group. This only affects email membership, not access.
4746.technical_description: Security event 4746: member added to a security-disabled local group.

where.Computer: Machine where the change was recorded

suspicious_when: Add of an unusual member to a sensitive mailing list

severity.high: Add to a sensitive mailing list

4746.important_note: Distribution groups do not grant resource access.

4750.headline: A distribution (non-security) global group was changed
4750.plain_english: A distribution (non-security) global group's properties were changed.
4750.technical_description: Security event 4750: security-disabled global group changed.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

suspicious_when: Unexplained changes

severity.high: Change to a group used by an admin process

4750.important_note: Distribution groups do not grant access.

4751.headline: Someone was added to a distribution global group
4751.plain_english: Someone was added to a distribution (non-security) global group.
4751.technical_description: Security event 4751: member added to a security-disabled global group.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

suspicious_when: Unexplained add to a sensitive mailing list

severity.high: Add to a sensitive mailing list

4751.important_note: Distribution groups do not grant access.

4752.headline: Someone was removed from a distribution global group
4752.plain_english: Someone was removed from a distribution (non-security) global group.
4752.technical_description: Security event 4752: member removed from a security-disabled global group.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

suspicious_when: Unexplained removal

severity.high: Removal from a sensitive mailing list

4752.important_note: Distribution groups do not grant access.

4754.headline: A universal security group was created
4754.plain_english: A new universal security group was created. Universal groups grant access across multiple domains.
4754.technical_description: Security event 4754: security-enabled universal group created.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the creation

4754.why_it_matters: Universal groups can grant cross-domain access — a high-value target in multi-domain environments.
suspicious_when: Group created with admin-like name
Group created off-hours
Members added immediately
what_to_do: Confirm the creation with the AD admin

severity.high: Admin-sounding group or immediate population

4755.headline: A universal security group was changed
4755.plain_english: A universal security group's properties were changed.
4755.technical_description: Security event 4755: security-enabled universal group changed.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

suspicious_when: Unexplained change to a sensitive group

severity.high: Sensitive group changed without a ticket

4756.headline: Someone was added to a universal security group
4756.plain_english: Someone was added to a universal security group — this grants cross-domain access.
4756.technical_description: Security event 4756: member added to a security-enabled universal group.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

4756.why_it_matters: Universal group membership can be equivalent to admin access in multi-domain setups.
suspicious_when: Add to a highly privileged universal group without a ticket

severity.high: Add to a privileged universal group

4756.important_note: Universal group membership is a privilege escalation route.

4757.headline: Someone was removed from a universal security group
4757.plain_english: Someone was removed from a universal security group.
4757.technical_description: Security event 4757: member removed from a security-enabled universal group.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the removal

suspicious_when: Removal from a sensitive group without a ticket

severity.high: Removal from a critical group

4757.important_note: Removal from a critical group can disrupt operations.

4760.headline: A distribution universal group was changed
4760.plain_english: A distribution (non-security) universal group's properties were changed.
4760.technical_description: Security event 4760: security-disabled universal group changed.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

suspicious_when: Unexplained change

severity.high: Sensitive group change

4760.important_note: Distribution groups do not grant access.

4761.headline: Someone was added to a distribution universal group
4761.plain_english: Someone was added to a distribution (non-security) universal group.
4761.technical_description: Security event 4761: member added to a security-disabled universal group.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

suspicious_when: Unexplained add

severity.high: Add to a sensitive list

4761.important_note: Distribution groups do not grant access.

4762.headline: Someone was removed from a distribution universal group
4762.plain_english: Someone was removed from a distribution (non-security) universal group.
4762.technical_description: Security event 4762: member removed from a security-disabled universal group.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the removal

suspicious_when: Unexplained removal

severity.high: Removal from a sensitive list

4762.important_note: Distribution groups do not grant access.

4764.headline: A group's type was changed
4764.plain_english: A group's type was changed — for example, from distribution to security. This can change whether the group grants access.
4764.technical_description: Security event 4764: a group's type was changed (distribution ↔ security, or scope change).

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

4764.why_it_matters: Converting a distribution group to a security group suddenly makes its members subject to any ACLs referencing that group.
suspicious_when: Unexpected conversion of a distribution group to security
Conversion of a group referenced by sensitive ACLs
what_to_do: Check what ACLs reference the group

severity.high: Conversion of a group referenced by admin ACLs

4764.important_note: Changing group type can grant access that didn't exist before.

4767.headline: A locked user account was unlocked
4767.plain_english: A locked-out user account was unlocked by an administrator. The user can now sign in again.

where.Computer: Machine where the unlock was recorded

4767.why_it_matters: Routine, but repeated lockouts and unlocks can indicate ongoing password guessing.
suspicious_when: Repeated lockouts and unlocks for the same account
Unlock during off-hours for a non-active user
what_to_do: Confirm the user requested the unlock
Check whether repeated failures (4625, 4771) preceded the lock

severity.high: Repeated unlocks correlating with failures

4767.important_note: Repeated lockouts can indicate an ongoing attack or stale credentials on another device.

4793.headline: The password policy checking API was called
4793.plain_english: An application checked a proposed password against the domain's password policy. Routine for apps that let users change or set passwords.
4793.technical_description: Security event 4793: the Password Policy Checking API was called by a process.

where.Computer: Machine where the check occurred

4793.why_it_matters: Usually benign, but unusual callers can indicate reconnaissance.
suspicious_when: Called by an unexpected process
Called at unusual scale
what_to_do: Confirm the calling process is expected

severity.high: Caller correlates with other suspicious activity

4793.important_note: Routine unless the caller is unexpected.

4794.headline: The DSRM administrator password was set
4794.plain_english: The Directory Services Restore Mode (DSRM) administrator password was changed. DSRM is an offline admin mode on domain controllers — this is a rare, high-impact operation.
4794.technical_description: Security event 4794: DSRM administrator password was set. High-value operation on domain controllers.

where.Computer: Domain controller where the password was set

4794.why_it_matters: DSRM password is a break-glass credential; unexpected changes can indicate misuse.
suspicious_when: Change with no change ticket
Change by a non-DC admin
Change off-hours
what_to_do: Confirm with the DC owner that the change was authorized

severity.high: Change by an unusual account or off-hours

4794.important_note: DSRM password changes are rare — investigate any unexplained change.

4797.headline: An attempt was made to query blank passwords
4797.plain_english: An attempt was made to find accounts with blank passwords. Attackers do this to find accounts with no password protection.
4797.technical_description: Security event 4797: attempt to query the existence of blank passwords.

where.Computer: Machine where the query occurred

4797.why_it_matters: Reconnaissance technique for finding weakly-protected accounts.
suspicious_when: Performed by a non-IT account
Performed from an unusual machine
what_to_do: If unexpected, treat as reconnaissance and escalate

severity.high: Query by an unexpected account or correlated with other reconnaissance

4797.important_note: Even a single query is worth reviewing in sensitive environments.

4798.headline: A user's local group membership was enumerated
4798.plain_english: Someone listed the local groups a specific user belongs to. This is a common admin action and also a common attacker reconnaissance step.
4798.technical_description: Security event 4798: a user's local group membership was enumerated.

where.Computer: Machine where the enumeration occurred

4798.why_it_matters: Reconnaissance for privilege escalation — often precedes lateral movement.
suspicious_when: Enumerated by a non-admin account
Enumerated at scale across many machines
what_to_do: Check whether the enumerating account shows other reconnaissance activity

severity.high: Enumeration by a non-admin or at scale

4798.important_note: One event is low-signal; many events from one account is reconnaissance.

4799.headline: A local group's membership was enumerated
4799.plain_english: Someone listed the members of a local security group. Same idea as the previous event but listing a group's members.
4799.technical_description: Security event 4799: a security-enabled local group's membership was enumerated.

where.Computer: Machine where the enumeration occurred

4799.why_it_matters: Reconnaissance for privilege escalation, especially enumeration of Administrators.
suspicious_when: Enumeration of Administrators by non-admin
Enumeration at scale
what_to_do: Review whether the enumerator did anything else afterward

severity.high: Enumeration of Administrators or at scale

4799.important_note: One event is low-signal; patterns matter.

implementation_notes.verified_field: Only display a plain-English explanation when `verified` is true.
